recognize_zh: 下方細胞為核偏心、有核周淡染區、細胞質深藍的漿細胞，細胞質內可見數條細長、紫紅色的棒狀包涵體（類 Auer 小體）與一顆小圓點；漿細胞中出現這種嗜天青棒狀結晶，提示骨髓瘤細胞內免疫球蛋白結晶化。
features: Lower cell: plasma cell with eccentric round nucleus, clumped chromatin and deep basophilic cytoplasm with perinuclear pallor
Several slender, needle-like azurophilic (pink-purple) rod-shaped intracytoplasmic inclusions overlying the perinuclear region, plus a small dot-like inclusion
Upper cell: round nucleus with abundant lilac cytoplasm containing fine granules; lineage uncertain in this single field (possibly an immature granulocyte or plasma cell with fine granulation)
Clean smear background with scattered red cells and platelet/stain debris; no other cells for context
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (May-Grunwald-Giemsa) shows a plasma cell with an eccentric nucleus, coarsely clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing several slender, rod-shaped azurophilic inclusions resembling Auer rods, together with a small round inclusion. An adjacent cell with a round nucleus and finely granular lilac cytoplasm is present, and its lineage cannot be established from this single field. Auer rod-like crystalline inclusions in plasma cells represent crystallized immunoglobulin (often kappa light chain) and, in the clinical context of IgG kappa myeloma, the findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma with Auer rod-like inclusions.

ddx.dx: Acute myeloid leukemia with Auer rods
ddx.vs: True Auer rods occur in MPO-positive myeloblasts with fine chromatin and nucleoli, whereas these rods lie in mature-appearing plasma cells with clumped chromatin and are MPO-negative.
Crystals accumulate in histiocytes (CD68/CD163-positive, abundant pale cytoplasm), not in basophilic plasma cells.

ddx.dx: Plasma cells with Russell bodies / Dutcher bodies
ddx.vs: Russell bodies are round globules and Dutcher bodies are intranuclear pseudoinclusions, not slender needle-shaped crystals.

ddx.dx: Acquired Fanconi syndrome-associated light-chain crystal myeloma
ddx.vs: Also has crystalline kappa inclusions; distinguished by proximal tubulopathy and needle crystals in renal tubular cells rather than by marrow morphology.
